q: How do I calculate CO2 per kg of glassware at an Ambala scientific glassware unit?
title: Ambala glassware: CO2 per kg
short: LPG burnt in lampworking burners and lehrs × 2.98 kg CO2 per kg of LPG, plus electricity × 0.710, divided by kg of good glassware. Bought borosilicate tubing carries its own footprint in Scope 3, often larger than your direct emissions.
audience: Scientific and laboratory glassware makers in Ambala

ul: LPG cylinders or bulk LPG, in kg, from invoices.
Oxygen used with LPG adds no CO2 itself.

p: Ask the tubing supplier for kg CO2 per kg, or use a glass factor labelled as an estimate.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record, so each figure shows the quantity, factor and document it came from.
